sections.context: Flick is 2.3k lines and about to absorb Hammerspoon, Hyperkey, an app manager, a herdr client, activity tracking, tasks and an agent bridge. Today every feature leaks into three shared places: the closed `search::Action` enum (every feature adds a variant), `app::State` (every feature adds fields and match arms in enter/refresh/render/activate), and `config::Config` (every feature adds top-level keys). Objective-C/unsafe code is spread across app.rs, ui.rs, windows.rs, spaces.rs. Each new feature would make all of these shallower and more entangled (APOSD: change amplification, cognitive load, information leakage). This refactor makes features deep, independent modules behind a narrow interface, isolates the platform, and adds a text interface (socket + CLI) so other programs and agents can compose with Flick (Unix philosophy).
sections.behavior_invariant: Everything a user can do today works identically: (1) all hotkeys in an existing config.toml (hotkey, desktop_toggle, windows_hotkey, [window_keys]) bind and behave the same, including repeat-to-cycle halves; (2) existing config.toml files parse unchanged — new per-module sections are additive, old top-level keys remain valid; (3) launcher ranking is unchanged: same fuzzy matching, same frecency, and item ids `app:<path>`, `window:<title>`, `quicklink:<name>`, `builtin:<title>` are preserved byte-for-byte so the `usage` table in an existing flick.db keeps its history; (4) clipboard history keeps its 500-clip cap, dedupe, concealed/transient skip, and paste-into-previous-app; existing `clips` rows survive; (5) window switcher order (previous window first, other-desktop apps collapsed) and desktop toggle behave the same; (6) `flick snapshot <png> [query]` and `flick import-raycast <file>` keep their arguments, output and exit codes; (7) single-instance check, Accessory activation policy, and no network access remain; (8) idle CPU stays ~0 and the release binary stays under 5 MB.
sections.approach:
Layered single crate, boundaries enforced by a check script (split into a cargo workspace only if compile times or boundary violations demand it).

Layout:
- `src/platform/` — the ONLY place with `unsafe`, objc2, Carbon, AX, CG, CF. Exposes safe, Flick-shaped functions (pasteboard, workspace, ax windows, spaces, hotkeys, timers, panel). Deep module: callers never see CF types or selectors.
- `src/core/` — pure Rust, no platform imports where avoidable: `Item`, `Ranker`/frecency, `Event`, `Module` trait, registry, `Store` (shared SQLite + per-module migrations), config loading, control protocol types. Unit-testable without AppKit.
- `src/modules/<name>/` — one directory per feature: apps, quicklinks, clipboard, windows (snap), switcher, desktop, flick (builtins). Modules depend on core + platform, never on each other.
- `src/ui/` — the panel view; renders a `ListView` and forwards keys. Knows nothing about features.
- `src/cli/` — argument parsing and the socket client.

Key interfaces (keep them small; push complexity down):
- `trait Module { fn id(&self) -> &'static str; fn items(&mut self, cx) -> Vec<Item> /* root search contributions */; fn open(&mut self, view, cx) -> Option<ListView> /* own list modes */; fn activate(&mut self, key: &str, cx) -> Outcome; fn on_event(&mut self, ev: &Event, cx) {} ; fn command(&mut self, args: &[String], cx) -> Result<String> {} /* socket/CLI verbs */ }`. Default methods do nothing, so a module implements only what it needs.
- `Item { id: ItemId { module, key }, title, subtitle, accessory, icon, keywords }` — no Action enum; activation routes to the owning module by id. `Outcome = Hide | Stay(status) | Push(ListView) | Pop`.
- `Event` enum (AppActivated, PasteboardChanged, Wake, Idle(secs), DisplaysChanged, Hotkey(binding), ...) produced by platform observers and dispatched synchronously on the main thread; background threads post to main via a channel + main-queue wakeup. No polling except where macOS forces it (pasteboard changeCount).
- Config: each module deserializes its own `[<module>]` table (with `enabled`), so module config types are private to the module. Legacy top-level keys are mapped in one place.
- Store: one connection; each module declares migrations keyed by module name in a `schema_versions` table. Modules own their tables; no cross-module SQL.
- Control socket: `~/Library/Application Support/Flick/flick.sock`, one request per line (`<module> <verb> [args...]` as JSON array), one JSON reply. `flick <module> <verb> ...` prints plain text, `--json` prints raw. `flick events` streams events as JSON lines for composition with other tools.
- Errors: one small `Error` type in core; modules surface errors as status text, never panic. Each module's event/command handlers are wrapped so a failure in one cannot take the launcher down.

Order: gates and characterization tests first, then move code without changing it (platform), then change interfaces one at a time, porting one module per step.

steps.title: Quality gates: Rust check:all (fmt, clippy pedantic subset, test, custom checks) + CI + pre-commit
Characterization tests: item ids, legacy config parsing, store schema, window rect math
Move all unsafe/objc2/CF/AX/Carbon code into src/platform with safe APIs; boundary check forbids unsafe elsewhere
Core types: ItemId-routed Item, Outcome, ListView, Module trait, registry; delete search::Action
Port features to src/modules: apps, quicklinks, clipboard, windows, switcher, desktop, flick builtins; app.rs becomes a thin view controller
Per-module config tables with enabled flag; legacy top-level keys mapped in one place
Store: shared connection, per-module migrations via schema_versions; existing usage/clips tables adopted
Event bus: platform observers (app activated, pasteboard, wake, displays, idle) dispatched to modules on main thread; panic isolation per handler
Control socket + CLI client: flick <module> <verb>, --json, flick events stream; fold snapshot/import-raycast into the same dispatcher
Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (layers, module contract, how to add a module); AGENTS.md conventions; mulch records

acceptance: Characterization tests from step 2 pass unchanged at every later step.
An existing ~/.config/flick/config.toml and flick.db load with no edits; frecency order for a fixed query matches pre-refactor.
`flick snapshot out.png ''` and `flick snapshot out.png vsc` produce visually identical PNGs before and after.
Boundary checks pass: `unsafe`/objc2 only under src/platform; no `crate::modules::` imports inside another module; no `crate::platform` imports in src/core.
Adding a toy module touches only src/modules/<toy>/ plus one registry line (verified by doing it in the docs step).
Manual smoke test on the installed app: launcher, quicklink keyword, clipboard paste, window switcher, snap + cycle, desktop toggle, reload config.
Release binary < 5 MB; idle CPU ~0% over 60 s in Activity Monitor.

name: Core: platform layer, modules, events, control socket

sections.context: Today a quicklink exists only if the user hand-edits ~/.config/flick/config.toml and runs Reload. Raycast users expect 'Create Quicklink' plus Edit/Delete on a quicklink. Flick has no way to take structured input: the only views are ListView (one search field + rows), there are no secondary actions on an item, and there is no confirmation step before a destructive action. Config is read with `toml` and the only writer (import-raycast) appends raw text. This plan adds three generic, reusable launcher capabilities (form view, per-item action menu, confirmation view), a comment-preserving config writer, and then uses them for the quicklink editor. The app manager epic (flick-7053) reuses the action menu and the confirmation view, so this plan lands its core/platform/controller steps first.
sections.approach:
Generic capabilities first, feature last. Each layer change is its own step and keeps the architecture rules: FFI only in src/platform, core pure, modules never import each other, Push-style requests by (module, name).

1. Core contract (src/core, pure, 100% coverage):
- `core::form`: `Form { module, name, title, fields: Vec<Field>, focused, submit_label, error: Option<String> }`, `Field { key: &'static str, label, value, placeholder, required: bool }`. Pure editing helpers: focus_next/prev (wrapping), set_value(index, text), value(key), missing_required().
- `core::action`: `Action { key: &'static str, title, icon: Icon, shortcut_hint: &'static str }`.
- `core::confirm`: `Confirm { module, token: String, title, lines: Vec<Item>-like rows (title, subtitle, accessory), confirm_label, destructive: bool }`.
- `Outcome::Form { module, name }` (a request, like Push, so `builtin` can open the quicklink form without importing it) and `Outcome::Confirm(Confirm)`.
- New `Module` methods with do-nothing defaults: `form(name, cx) -> Option<Form>`; `submit(&Form, cx) -> Result<String, String>` (Ok = status shown on root search, Err = inline error, form stays); `actions(&ItemId, cx) -> Vec<Action>` (computed lazily on cmd+K so state such as 'running' is fresh); `act(&ItemId, action_key, cx) -> Outcome`; `confirmed(token, cx) -> Outcome`. Registry routes each by module id; unknown module -> None/Stay(None). Not panic-isolated (same as activate).

2. Platform panel (src/platform/panel): form layout mode - a title label, up to 6 pre-created label + NSTextField rows shown/hidden per frame, an error line, footer; focus moves on Tab / Shift-Tab; a `field_changed(index)` handler and `field_value(index)` getter. New keys: `Key::BackTab` (insertBacktab:), `Key::CmdK` and `Key::CmdEnter` (via `performKeyEquivalent:` on the FlickPanel class; tail-expression returns, see mx-43d3f4). A way to make the search field read-only with a title (for confirm and action screens). Platform knows no core types: it takes its own `FormFrame` structs; callbacks are fn pointers in `Handlers` (mx-db09fc).

3. Config writer (src/config.rs + new src/config/edit.rs or src/config_edit.rs): add `toml_edit` (MIT/Apache-2.0, already allowed by deny.toml). API sketch: `config::edit_entries(module, key, op)` where op is `Append(entry) | Replace { name, entry } | Remove { name }` and entry is ordered `(field, string)` pairs. It edits the array of tables `[[<module>.<key>]]`; for Replace/Remove it also searches the legacy location from `LEGACY` (e.g. `[[quicklinks]]`) so legacy knowledge stays in config.rs. Appends always use the new table form. Comments, blank lines and key order elsewhere are byte-for-byte preserved. Writes are atomic (temp file in the same directory, fsync, rename), refuse when the file does not parse, and create the default file first if it is missing. Parses the result with `config::parse` before renaming, so a write can never leave an unloadable file.

4. UI + controller (src/ui.rs, src/app.rs, maybe new src/screen.rs): replace `view: Option<ListView>` with a `Screen` enum: Root | List(ListView) | Form(Form) | Actions { target: Item, back: Box<Screen>, items } | Confirm { confirm, back }. cmd+K on a selected row with actions opens the action list (typing filters it, Enter runs `act`, Escape returns to the previous screen with its query). Form: Tab/Shift-Tab move focus, Enter submits (missing required fields -> inline error without calling the module), Escape returns to root. Confirm: rows are read-only; non-destructive: Enter confirms; destructive: only cmd+Enter confirms, plain Enter shows 'Press ⌘↵ to <label>'; Escape cancels. Footer shows '⌘K Actions' when the selected item has actions (ask lazily; cheap). Update ARCHITECTURE.md (Module contract table, Outcome list, 'There is no Pop' paragraph) in the same commit.

5. Quicklink open-with app: `Quicklink.app: Option<String>` (app name or .app path, serde skip-if-none) and `platform::workspace::open_url_with(url, app)` via NSWorkspace openURLs:withApplicationAtURL:configuration:completionHandler: (resolve a bare name through /Applications lookups or `URLForApplicationWithBundleIdentifier`). Unknown app -> status error, not a panic.

6. Quicklink editor (src/modules/quicklinks + one builtin item): builtin item 'Create Quicklink' returns `Outcome::Form { module: "quicklink", name: "new" }`; quicklink owns forms `new` and `edit/<name>` (form names are a separate namespace from list views, so no clash with link-named views). Fields: Name (required), URL or path (required, hint '{query} for an argument'), Keyword (optional), Open with (optional app). Actions on a quicklink item: Open (primary), Edit Quicklink, Delete Quicklink, Copy URL is out of scope. Delete -> Confirm (non-destructive Enter, it only edits config). Validation (pure, unit-tested in a new validate.rs): trimmed non-empty name and URL; name unique case-insensitively (excluding the link being edited; consistent with flick-abe2); keyword has no spaces and is not used by another link; URL must contain '://' or start with '/' or '~/'. On success the module writes through the config writer and updates its own in-memory `links` (no global reload, so hotkeys are not rebound and the launcher stays open), then returns to root with 'Saved quicklink <name>'. CLI parity: `flick quicklink add <name> <url> [--keyword k] [--app a]`, `quicklink remove <name>`, `quicklink list`; `verbs()` lists them.

Parallelism: steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are independent and can run concurrently. Step 4 needs 1 and 2. Step 6 needs 3, 4 and 5.

Cross-plan ordering: this plan owns the shared action menu and confirmation view. flick-7053 (app manager) steps that add app actions and the uninstall confirmation depend on steps 1, 2 and 4 of this plan; after both plans are submitted, add `sd dep add` from those flick-7053 children to step 4's child.

Defaults chosen: 'Create Quicklink' lives in `builtin` (id `builtin:Create Quicklink`) because any `quicklink:<key>` could collide with a user's link name; this extends the pinned builtin list in src/characterization/item_ids.rs (additive behavior change, say so in the commit). Renaming a link changes its id `quicklink:<name>`, so its frecency starts over.

alternatives.name: Hand-rolled text editing of config.toml (find the [[...]] block by regex, splice lines)
alternatives.rejected_because: Fragile with inline tables, comments between keys, legacy [[quicklinks]] and multi-line strings; toml_edit is the standard format-preserving editor and reuses the same TOML grammar.

alternatives.name: Store quicklinks in SQLite (store.rs) instead of config.toml
alternatives.rejected_because: Splits the source of truth: users and import-raycast edit config.toml, and the dotfiles workflow versions it. The seed asks for config.toml.

alternatives.name: Re-serialize the whole config with toml::to_string after editing
alternatives.rejected_because: Drops every comment and reorders keys, destroying the commented default config the first run writes.

alternatives.name: Model the form as a ListView where each row is a field edited through the single search field
alternatives.rejected_because: No visible state for the other fields, awkward Tab semantics, and it cannot show labels plus values at once; a real form layout is reusable by future modules (tasks, herdr).

alternatives.name: Outcome::Form(Form) carrying the full form instead of a (module, name) request
alternatives.rejected_because: Then `builtin` would have to build the quicklink form, i.e. know quicklink fields; a request by name keeps modules independent, like Push.

alternatives.name: Finish with Outcome::ReloadConfig after every save
alternatives.rejected_because: Reload rebinds every hotkey and resets the screen; the module already knows the exact change, so updating its in-memory list is cheaper and works the same for socket commands, which cannot return an Outcome.

alternatives.name: Put the action menu and confirmation view in the app manager plan
alternatives.rejected_because: Quicklink Edit/Delete needs both too and this plan is smaller, so it can land the shared pieces sooner.

steps.title: Core: Form, Action and Confirm types; Outcome::Form/Confirm; Module form/submit/actions/act/confirmed with registry routing (pure, 100% coverage)
Platform panel: form layout (labelled text fields, focus, error line), read-only title mode, keys Shift-Tab, cmd+K and cmd+Enter
Config writer: toml_edit, comment-preserving, atomic, legacy-aware append/replace/remove of [[<module>.<key>]] entries
Controller + ui: Screen enum with form, cmd+K action menu and confirm screens; ARCHITECTURE.md contract update
Quicklink 'Open with' app: Quicklink.app field and platform::workspace::open_url_with
Quicklink editor: Create Quicklink form, Edit/Delete actions, validation, save via config writer, CLI quicklink add/remove/list

risks: ASSUMPTION: 'Create Quicklink' is a builtin root item (builtin:Create Quicklink). It changes the pinned builtin list in src/characterization/item_ids.rs; the commit must call this out as an additive behavior change. With [quicklink] enabled = false, activating it shows a status line instead of a form.
ASSUMPTION: saving updates the quicklink module's in-memory links and does not run a full config reload; a user who hand-edits config.toml meanwhile still needs Reload Flick Config.
ASSUMPTION: renaming a quicklink changes its id quicklink:<name>, so its frecency history starts over (usage table is keyed by id; no migration of usage rows).
ASSUMPTION: Delete Quicklink asks for confirmation with plain Enter (non-destructive: it only edits config). Destructive confirms (uninstall) require cmd+Enter.
ASSUMPTION: 'Open with' accepts an app name (matched like `flick app open`) or a .app path; it is stored as given.
ASSUMPTION: Edit/Delete of a link that lives in a legacy [[quicklinks]] table edits it in place there; it is not migrated to [[quicklink.links]]. New links always go to [[quicklink.links]].

cmd+K / cmd+Enter: NSTextField's field editor may consume key equivalents before the panel; performKeyEquivalent: on FlickPanel must return true only for handled keys, or system shortcuts (cmd+C/V/A in the field) break. Smoke-test copy/paste in the field.
define_class! methods cannot early-return false (mx-43d3f4); use tail expressions in performKeyEquivalent:.
app.rs is 321 lines; the Screen enum and three new screens can push it over the 500-line check:size budget. Put pure screen state/transition code in a new file (mx-e7e3ab); never raise a budget.
Core coverage floor is 100% (scripts/coverage-budgets.json 'src/core/'); every new core branch needs a unit test.
toml_edit adds a second TOML parser to the binary; check:binary-size ceiling is 5 MB and the release binary is ~3.7 MB. Disable default features not needed (e.g. keep only 'parse' and 'display').
Atomic rename replaces a symlinked config.toml with a regular file. Resolve the symlink (fs::canonicalize) and write next to the target; dotfile setups often symlink it.
A write that races a hand edit loses one of them; re-read and parse the file immediately before editing, never cache the document.
Panel focus: switching between the search field and form fields must keep the panel key window; windowDidResignKey hides the launcher, so never make a non-panel window key.
Modules never import each other: builtin opens the form only through Outcome::Form { module: "quicklink", name: "new" }; check:layers enforces it.
acceptance: scripts/check-all.sh passes after every step; no file-size, coverage or binary-size budget is raised.
src/core coverage stays 100%; unit tests cover Form focus wrap, required-field detection, registry routing of form/submit/actions/act/confirmed to the owning module, and unknown-module fallbacks.

Config writer tests: on DEFAULT_CONFIG plus a hand-commented fixture, Append/Replace/Remove change only the targeted entry (diff of the rest of the file is empty); comments and blank lines survive; Replace/Remove find an entry under legacy [[quicklinks]]; a write whose result would not parse is refused and leaves the file untouched; a symlinked config is written through to its target.
Validation tests: empty name, empty URL, duplicate name (any case), keyword with a space, keyword used by another link, editing a link keeps its own name/keyword valid.

`flick quicklink add Docs https://docs.rs/{query} --keyword d` exits 0, appends a [[quicklink.links]] entry, and `d serde` in root search opens immediately without a reload; `flick quicklink add Docs x` fails with a duplicate-name error and exit 1; `flick quicklink remove Docs` removes it; `flick help` lists the new verbs.
ARCHITECTURE.md documents Outcome::Form, Outcome::Confirm, the new Module methods and the Screen behavior (action menu Escape returns to the previous screen) in the same commit as step 4.
Existing characterization tests pass unchanged, except the builtin id list in item_ids.rs, which gains 'builtin:Create Quicklink' (commit message says so).

Manual smoke (installed app): (1) type 'create quick', Enter -> form with 4 fields, focus in Name; (2) Tab/Shift-Tab cycle fields; Enter with empty URL shows an inline error; (3) fill Name 'Crates', URL 'https://crates.io/search?q={query}', Keyword 'cr', Enter -> back at root with 'Saved quicklink Crates'; 'cr tokio' opens crates.io; (4) select Crates, cmd+K -> Edit/Delete actions; Edit shows prefilled values; change keyword to 'crt', save, 'crt x' works and 'cr x' no longer does; (5) cmd+K -> Delete -> confirm screen, Escape cancels (link still there), repeat and Enter -> link gone; (6) config.toml comments unchanged (git diff / diff against a copy shows only the edited entry); (7) a link with Open with 'Safari' opens in Safari while another browser is default; (8) cmd+C / cmd+V / cmd+A still work in the search field and in form fields; (9) Escape from the form returns to root; the launcher hotkey toggles as before; (10) Reload Flick Config still works after edits.

name: Forms, action menu, confirm; quicklink editor

sections.context: The app module only lists installed apps and opens them (src/modules/apps/mod.rs). Quitting, force-quitting, revealing in Finder and uninstalling all mean leaving the launcher for Finder, Activity Monitor or a third-party uninstaller (AppCleaner). Flick should do these from an app item, like Raycast. Uninstall is the risky part: deleting the wrong path loses user data. So it must move items to the Trash (recoverable, never rm), show exactly what will go before anything happens, find leftovers conservatively (bundle-id names only, inside a fixed set of ~/Library folders), and refuse system apps. This plan builds on the generic action menu (cmd+K) and confirmation screen delivered by the flick-32a7 plan.
sections.approach:
Prerequisite (cross-plan): the flick-32a7 plan must land its steps 1 (core Action/Confirm + Module actions/act/confirmed), 2 (panel keys cmd+K, cmd+Enter) and 4 (controller action menu and confirm screens) before steps 4 and 5 here start. After both plans are submitted, run `sd dep add <this plan's step-4 child> <flick-32a7 step-4 child>` and the same for step 5. Steps 1, 2, 3 and 6 here do not need the other plan.

All new FFI goes in src/platform; everything else is in src/modules/apps (split into files to stay under 500 lines: mod.rs, actions.rs, running.rs, leftovers.rs, uninstall.rs). Item ids stay `app:<bundle path>` (pinned).

1. Platform app control (src/platform/workspace.rs, new fns): `bundle_id(path) -> Option<String>` (NSBundle bundleWithPath / bundleIdentifier), `running_for_bundle(path) -> Vec<i32>`, `terminate(pid) -> bool` (NSRunningApplication terminate: polite, like cmd+Q, the app may ask to save), `force_terminate(pid) -> bool` (forceTerminate), `reveal(path)` (NSWorkspace activateFileViewerSelectingURLs). Expose Flick's own bundle path from platform::app so the module can protect itself.
2. Platform trash (new src/platform/files.rs): `trash(path) -> Result<PathBuf, String>` using NSFileManager trashItemAtURL:resultingItemURL:error:, returning the item's new location in the Trash; the NSError's localized description becomes the Err text. No other delete primitive is added anywhere.
3. Pure leftovers + protection (src/modules/apps/leftovers.rs, no platform calls; home dir and bundle id are parameters so tests use a temp dir): roots are exactly ~/Library/{Application Support, Caches, Preferences, Containers, Group Containers, Saved Application State, LaunchAgents, Logs, HTTPStorages, WebKit}. Matching is exact on the bundle id `bid`: `<bid>` (any root), `<bid>.plist` (Preferences, LaunchAgents), `Preferences/ByHost/<bid>.<hardware-uuid>.plist`, `<bid>.savedState` (Saved Application State), `<bid>.binarycookies` (HTTPStorages), and in Group Containers `<TEAMID>.<bid>` or `group.<bid>`. Case-sensitive. No prefix matching (com.google.Chrome must not match com.google.Chrome.canary), no app-name matching. Entries are read with symlink_metadata: symlinks are never followed and a symlink entry is skipped; every result must be a direct child of an allowed root (or of Preferences/ByHost) after canonicalizing the root. Sizes are summed with a non-following walk. `protected(app_path, bid, own_bundle) -> Option<reason>`: path under /System or /Library/Apple, bid empty or starting with `com.apple.`, Flick itself, or a path outside /Applications, ~/Applications and their one-level subfolders. Add a 100% (or measured) floor for this file to scripts/coverage-budgets.json (tightening only).
4. App actions (src/modules/apps/actions.rs) via `Module::actions`/`act`: Open Application (primary Enter, unchanged), Show in Finder, Quit (only when running), Force Quit (only when running), Uninstall… (hidden for protected apps). CLI: `app quit <name>`, `app force-quit <name>`, `app reveal <name>`; update `verbs()`.
5. Uninstall (src/modules/apps/uninstall.rs): Uninstall… computes the plan (app bundle + leftovers + sizes) and returns `Outcome::Confirm` with destructive = true: title 'Uninstall <App>', one read-only row per path with its size, a total, and confirm label 'Move N items (X MB) to Trash'; only cmd+Enter confirms. The module stores the exact list under the confirm token; on `confirmed` it trashes exactly that list (re-checking each path is still an allowed match and still exists; changed paths are skipped and reported). The app bundle is trashed first; if that fails, nothing else is touched. Leftover failures do not stop the others; the status line reports counts and the first error. A running app is refused ('Quit <App> first'). Afterward the app index rescans. CLI: `app uninstall <name> --dry-run` prints `<size>\t<path>` lines and a total, exit 0; `app uninstall <name> --yes` performs it and prints what moved; with neither flag it prints the list and fails ('pass --yes to move these to the Trash'), exit 1.
6. Running Applications view (src/modules/apps/running.rs): a root item 'Quit Applications' (id `app:quit` - safe because app keys are absolute paths starting with '/') opens view `app/running` listing running regular apps (platform::workspace::regular_apps) with their icons; Enter quits the selected app (id `app:<path>` with arg 'quit'), cmd+K gives the step-4 actions (Force Quit etc.). The view refreshes on `AppActivated` events. CLI `app running` prints `<pid>\t<name>\t<path>`. The existing `app list` covers the installed-app list.

Parallelism: steps 1, 2 and 3 can run concurrently (and concurrently with all of flick-32a7). Step 6 needs only step 1. Step 4 needs step 1 plus flick-32a7 step 4. Step 5 needs 2, 3 and 4 plus flick-32a7 step 4. Steps 5 and 6 can run concurrently.

alternatives.name: Delete with std::fs::remove_dir_all / rm
alternatives.rejected_because: Unrecoverable; one wrong match destroys user data. The Trash keeps every uninstall reversible and the seed requires trashItemAtURL.

alternatives.name: AppCleaner-style fuzzy matching (app name, vendor name, bundle-id prefixes)
alternatives.rejected_because: Finds more leftovers but also other apps' data (Chrome vs Chrome Canary, 'Code' folders). Conservative exact bundle-id matching was requested; missed leftovers are harmless, wrong ones are not.

alternatives.name: Scan /Library (system-wide) and privileged helpers too
alternatives.rejected_because: Needs admin rights and touches other users' data; out of scope. Only the user's ~/Library roots listed in the seed.

alternatives.name: Quit the app automatically before uninstalling
alternatives.rejected_because: Quitting can lose unsaved work and the app may refuse; refusing with 'Quit <App> first' keeps the destructive flow to one explicit decision.

alternatives.name: Plain Enter to confirm uninstall
alternatives.rejected_because: Enter is the key the user just pressed to choose Uninstall…; a double press would trash data. cmd+Enter makes the destructive confirm a deliberate, different key.

alternatives.name: A separate 'manage apps' module
alternatives.rejected_because: It would duplicate the app index and could not import the apps module; the features act on app:<path> items, so they belong to the app module.

steps.title: Platform: bundle id lookup, running pids per bundle, terminate/force-terminate, reveal in Finder, Flick's own bundle path
Platform: files::trash via NSFileManager trashItemAtURL (the only delete primitive)
Apps: pure leftover finder (exact bundle-id matches in the ~/Library roots, no symlinks, sizes) and system-app protection, with temp-dir tests
Apps: action menu on app items (Show in Finder, Quit, Force Quit) + CLI app quit/force-quit/reveal (needs flick-32a7 step 4)
Apps: Uninstall with confirm screen (paths + sizes, cmd+Enter), trash exactly the listed paths, CLI app uninstall --dry-run/--yes (needs flick-32a7 step 4)
Apps: Quit Applications view of running apps (Enter quits) + CLI app running

risks: ASSUMPTION: leftovers are exact bundle-id names only; folders named after the app (e.g. ~/Library/Application Support/Slack) and bundle-id-prefixed helpers (com.foo.App.helper) are not found. Some data stays behind; this is the conservative trade-off.
ASSUMPTION: uninstalling a running app is refused with 'Quit <App> first'; it is not quit automatically.
ASSUMPTION: destructive confirmation needs cmd+Enter (plain Enter shows a hint); Escape cancels. The CLI needs --yes to act, --dry-run only lists.

ASSUMPTION: protected = anything under /System or /Library/Apple, any com.apple.* bundle id, apps with no bundle id, Flick itself, and apps outside /Applications and ~/Applications (plus one subfolder level, matching the scan). Protected apps show no Uninstall action and the CLI refuses them.
ASSUMPTION: no privilege escalation. Root-owned or App Store apps that the user cannot trash fail with the system's error text ('use Finder'); leftovers are then untouched.
ASSUMPTION: 'list' is covered by the existing root items and `app list`, plus the new Quit Applications view and `app running`; no separate installed-apps manager view.

Cross-plan dependency: steps 4 and 5 cannot start until flick-32a7 steps 1, 2 and 4 are merged (Module::actions/act/confirmed, cmd+K/cmd+Enter, controller screens). Add the sd deps after submitting both plans.

Containers and Group Containers are protected by macOS (App Management / container privacy on macOS 14+); trashItemAtURL can fail or trigger a TCC prompt. Report per-path failures; never retry with another delete method.

A confirm token that outlives a change (app updated, leftover replaced by a symlink) could trash something not shown: re-validate every stored path against the same matching rules and symlink_metadata just before trashing, skip and report any that changed.

Sizing a large Containers folder can take seconds on the main thread and freeze the launcher. Cap the walk (e.g. stop at 200k entries and show '>= X') or compute in a background thread and post the confirm back with platform::events::on_main (mx-1d2d92); never touch module state off-main.
Bundle id lookup per app during scan() on every LauncherOpened would slow the launcher; look it up lazily (on cmd+K / uninstall), not in scan().
Quit (terminate) is asynchronous and can be vetoed by the app; report 'Asked <App> to quit', not 'Quit'. Force Quit loses unsaved data: show it only for running apps and label it clearly.

Item id format app:<path> and the pinned root ordering in src/characterization must not change; the 'Quit Applications' root item (app:quit) extends the app items — check ranking/item_ids characterization tests and call out any changed assertion in the commit.
check:size: apps/mod.rs is 141 lines today; keep new code in separate files. Coverage floors only tighten.
acceptance: scripts/check-all.sh passes after every step; no budget raised; check:layers shows no unsafe/objc2 outside src/platform and no cross-module imports.
grep shows no remove_file/remove_dir/remove_dir_all/`rm` in src/modules/apps or src/platform/files.rs; platform::files::trash is the only removal path used by uninstall.

Leftover finder unit tests (temp HOME): for bid dev.flick.test it finds Caches/dev.flick.test, Preferences/dev.flick.test.plist, Preferences/ByHost/dev.flick.test.<UUID>.plist, Saved Application State/dev.flick.test.savedState, HTTPStorages/dev.flick.test.binarycookies, Group Containers/ABCDE12345.dev.flick.test, LaunchAgents/dev.flick.test.plist; it ignores dev.flick.test2, dev.flick.test.helper, DEV.FLICK.TEST, a folder named after the app, a symlink named dev.flick.test pointing outside ~/Library, and anything in ~/Library roots not on the list; sizes match the bytes written.

name: App manager: actions, running apps, safe uninstall

sections.context: Agents commit to the local checkout (~/Projects/flick), often ahead of GitHub. Today the only way to run that code is to ask an agent, or open a terminal, and run `scripts/bundle.sh --install`. That script builds, then does `pkill -x Flick; rm -rf ~/Applications/Flick.app; cp -R; open` (or `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<uid>/org.nix-community.home.flick` when the home-manager agent exists). It has three gaps: (1) the running app cannot tell which commit it is (Cargo.toml version is 0.0.1 forever, no sha is baked in), so nobody can see whether the checkout is ahead; (2) install is rm-then-copy, so a failed copy leaves no app; (3) it builds the working tree as is, so uncommitted agent edits leak into a 'clean' install. Flick should rebuild itself from the checkout's HEAD (or the dirty tree on request), report what is installed versus what is in the checkout, and never touch the network (no git fetch/pull/push; README promises Flick 'sends nothing over the network').
sections.approach:
A new module with id `flick` (directory `src/modules/rebuild/`, registry line `mod rebuild => "flick", rebuild::Rebuild::default;`). The existing `builtin` module (`src/modules/flick/`) is not touched; the id `flick` gives the seed's `[flick] source = ...` table and `flick flick rebuild|version` CLI for free. Item ids are permanent: `flick:version`, `flick:rebuild`, `flick:rebuild-dirty`, `flick:rebuild-available`, `flick:build-log`, `flick:cancel-build`.

Build stamp (contract shared by steps 1 and 3): `scripts/bundle.sh` exports `FLICK_BUILD_SHA` (full sha), `FLICK_BUILD_DIRTY` (`1`/`0`), `FLICK_BUILD_TIME` (RFC 3339 UTC) and `FLICK_BUILD_SOURCE` (absolute checkout path) before `cargo build`; each defaults to the value computed from the checkout (`git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain`) but a caller may pre-set it (Flick does, because an exported tree has no .git). The module reads them with `option_env!` into a pure `Stamp` (plain `cargo build`/tests give sha `dev`, source = `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`). Cargo tracks `option_env!` vars, so a changed stamp recompiles the crate. No build.rs: it would need rerun-if-changed on .git internals, which differ in worktrees. Info.plist `CFBundleVersion` becomes `<version>+<short sha>[-dirty]`.

Safe install (step 1): `bundle.sh` gains `--install` semantics that never leave a half-installed app: copy the built bundle to `~/Applications/.Flick.app.new`, verify `codesign --verify`, then `mv Flick.app .Flick.app.old && mv .Flick.app.new Flick.app && rm -rf .Flick.app.old` (renaming a running bundle is safe on macOS). Restart moves to `scripts/relaunch.sh [--wait-pid PID]`: with the launchd agent, `launchctl kickstart -k`; without it, `kill PID`, poll `kill -0` up to 10 s (then `kill -9`), then `open`. Waiting for the old pid keeps `platform::app::already_running()` from making the new copy exit with 'already running'. `bundle.sh --install` calls relaunch.sh, so the terminal path and the in-app path share one installer.

Version info (step 3): pure functions in `src/modules/rebuild/git.rs` parse the output of local-only git commands: `git -C <src> rev-parse HEAD`, `git rev-list --count <installed>..HEAD`, `git log --format=%h%x09%s <installed>..HEAD -n 5`, `git status --porcelain`. A fixed allow-list of git subcommands (`rev-parse`, `rev-list`, `log`, `status`, `archive`, `merge-base`) is enforced by one `git()` helper and pinned by a unit test, so fetch/pull/push/clone cannot appear. Checks run on a background thread on `Event::LauncherOpened` and `Event::Wake`, at most once per 30 s, results in an `Arc<Mutex<GitStatus>>`; `items()` reads the cache, so the main thread never waits on git. 'Flick Version' subtitle: `<short sha>[-dirty] built <time>` plus `3 commits newer in ~/Projects/flick: <subjects>`; 'Rebuild Available' appears only when installed sha != checkout HEAD. Never rebuilds automatically.

Progress (step 2, core): a new `Event::ModuleChanged { module: &'static str }` (stays `Copy`, serializes as `{"event":"module_changed","module":"flick"}`). A background thread posts it with `platform::events::post`; `on_event` returns true for its own module, so the controller refreshes a visible view of that module. This is the general 'my background work progressed' signal other modules (herdr, activity) will also need.

Rebuild runner (step 4): activating Rebuild pushes view `flick/build`, which lists 'Building <short sha>… 42s', the last log line, 'Cancel Build', 'Open Build Log'. One build at a time (second request: 'already building'). Thread: (a) HEAD build: `git -C <src> archive --format=tar HEAD | tar -x -C ~/Library/Caches/Flick/rebuild/src` (cleaned first), then `<export>/scripts/bundle.sh` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<src>/target/flick-rebuild`, `FLICK_BUILD_*` preset from the checkout; (b) dirty build: `<src>/scripts/bundle.sh` in the checkout with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<src>/target/flick-rebuild`, `FLICK_BUILD_DIRTY=1`. Using a separate target subdirectory avoids lock contention with agents running cargo in `target/` and keeps compiled deps warm across rebuilds. Commands run via the user's login shell (`$SHELL -lc`, fallback /bin/zsh) so PATH contains cargo/git even when launchd started Flick with a bare PATH. `cargo build --release --locked --offline`; with `[flick] gates = true` it runs `scripts/check-all.sh --bail` first. Output goes to `~/Library/Logs/Flick/rebuild.log` (previous kept as rebuild.log.1). While building, the thread posts `ModuleChanged` once per second (only during a build; idle cost stays zero). On failure: status 'Build failed (see log)', `open -t` the log, installed app untouched. On success: spawn `relaunch.sh --install <built .app> --wait-pid <our pid>` with `CommandExt::process_group(0)` (own process group, so launchd's kill of the Flick job does not kill it; no `unsafe`, no setsid FFI), stdout to the log, then return `Outcome::Hide` and let the helper restart Flick. Cancel kills the child's process group.

CLI parity (step 4): `flick flick version` (installed stamp + checkout status, synchronous git with a 2 s timeout because it runs off the user's request), `flick flick rebuild [--dirty] [--ref <rev>] [--source <dir>]` (returns immediately: `building <sha>; log: <path>`), `flick flick status` (idle | building Ns | failed | installing). `--ref` exports any local rev with `git archive`; `--source` builds another worktree (e.g. an agent's `agent/<branch>` worktree) to try it before merging. These two cover the seed's optional 'other branch or worktree' item without UI.

Config: `[flick] source = "~/Projects/flick"` (tilde expanded; default the baked `FLICK_BUILD_SOURCE`), `gates = false`, `check_on_open = true`. Unknown keys are errors like other modules.

Order and parallelism: steps 1, 2 and 3 are independent and can run concurrently (step 1 is shell only; step 2 is core only; step 3 adds the module with the stamp reader and git status, without building). Step 4 needs all three. Step 5 (docs and smoke) runs last.

Defaults chosen for open questions: dirty build is a separate root item 'Rebuild Flick (Dirty)', not a modifier key, because the panel has no modifier-activation path (`panel::Key`); gates are opt-in because check-all.sh runs coverage and cargo-deny (minutes, and deny may need its advisory DB); offline cargo is the default because the seed forbids network.

alternatives.name: git pull / fetch origin, then build
alternatives.rejected_because: The seed's premise: local commits are ahead of origin; pulling misses or conflicts with that work, and Flick promises no network.

alternatives.name: build.rs that runs git to bake the sha
alternatives.rejected_because: Needs rerun-if-changed on .git/HEAD and refs, which are files in a different place in worktrees and in an exported tree (no .git at all). Env vars set by bundle.sh work in all three, and cargo already tracks option_env! inputs.

alternatives.name: Build HEAD in a temporary `git worktree add --detach`
alternatives.rejected_because: Writes worktree metadata into the user's .git and collides with agents' worktree management; `git archive HEAD | tar -x` is read-only on the repo.

alternatives.name: Replace the running binary in place and exec() it
alternatives.rejected_because: Breaks the codesign seal of the running bundle and fights launchd's KeepAlive; a bundle swap plus a detached relaunch helper reuses the restart path bundle.sh already has.

alternatives.name: Auto-rebuild when the checkout moves
alternatives.rejected_because: Seed says never rebuild automatically; agents commit broken intermediate states.

alternatives.name: Progress via a polling timer in the module
alternatives.rejected_because: Polling costs idle CPU; a Copy event posted only while a build runs costs nothing when idle and is reusable by later modules.

steps.title: bundle.sh: FLICK_BUILD_* stamp env, atomic bundle swap, scripts/relaunch.sh that waits for the old pid (no half-installed app)
Core: Event::ModuleChanged { module } for background progress; controller refreshes the module's visible view
Module `flick` (src/modules/rebuild): build stamp via option_env!, [flick] source config, local-git status cache, Flick Version / Rebuild Available items, `flick flick version`
Rebuild runner: background build of HEAD (git archive) or dirty tree, progress view, log file, cancel, detached relaunch helper; `flick flick rebuild [--dirty] [--ref] [--source]` and `status`
Docs + smoke: README (Rebuild, [flick] table, relaunch), ARCHITECTURE (ModuleChanged, background-thread pattern), DEFAULT_CONFIG; run the manual smoke checklist

risks: Launchd PATH: a launchd-started Flick has PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:..., so `cargo` and nix-installed `git` are not found. Mitigation: run every build command through `$SHELL -lc`; the build view shows 'cargo not found on login-shell PATH' instead of a raw spawn error.

Relaunch race / single instance: if the new Flick starts before the old exits, `already_running()` makes the new one exit and the user has no launcher. Mitigation: relaunch.sh waits on the old pid (kill -0 loop, 10 s, then kill -9) before `open`; with the launchd agent, `kickstart -k` serializes it. Smoke-check `pgrep -x Flick | wc -l` == 1.

Helper killed with its parent: launchd kills the whole process group of the job on `kickstart -k`/exit. Mitigation: spawn relaunch.sh with `process_group(0)` and stdin/stdout detached; verify by rebuilding under the home-manager launchd agent.

Half install: a crash between the two `mv`s leaves `.Flick.app.old` and no `Flick.app`. Mitigation: relaunch.sh restores `.Flick.app.old` when `Flick.app` is missing at start; both renames are on one volume (atomic).

Accessibility / TCC grants reset if the signing identity changes (ad-hoc signing changes every build). Mitigation: keep bundle.sh's Apple Development identity lookup; the build view warns 'ad-hoc signed: macOS will ask for Accessibility again'. codesign from a launchd process may show a one-time keychain 'allow' dialog.
Agents editing the checkout during a dirty build: the dirty build captures a moving tree. Accepted: dirty is explicitly 'as it is now'; HEAD builds export a snapshot first and are unaffected.
Cargo lock contention / disk: a separate `target/flick-rebuild` doubles build artifacts (~1 GB). Accepted for no contention with agents' `target/`; `cargo clean --target-dir` documented.
`--offline` fails when an agent added a crate that was never fetched. Mitigation: the log tail says 'run `cargo fetch` in <source>'; Flick itself never fetches.

Main-thread stalls: git or cargo must never run on the main thread (a stalled main thread freezes the launcher and hotkeys). Only `flick flick version` runs git synchronously, with a 2 s timeout; everything else is on a thread and posts back via events::post / on_main (mulch mx-1d2d92).
Panic isolation: activate/items are not panic-isolated (mulch mx-2290b1); all spawn/IO errors become Outcome::Stay(Some(text)), never unwrap.
check:size: keep each new file under 500 lines (mulch mx-e7e3ab); split git parsing (git.rs), stamp (stamp.rs) and runner (build.rs) from mod.rs.

Dead code between steps: a pub item that only a later step uses (Event::ModuleChanged before step 4) fails lint as never constructed. Mitigation: `#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = "used by the rebuild runner, flick-b50f"))]`, removed in step 4 (an unfulfilled expect then fails, which forces the removal).
Module id `flick` vs CLI: `flick flick ...` must route to the module; verify cli::parse does not special-case the word (it special-cases only help/events/snapshot/import-raycast/reload).
ASSUMPTION: dirty build is a separate item 'Rebuild Flick (Dirty)' (and `--dirty` on the CLI), not a modifier key on Enter.
ASSUMPTION: quality gates before install are opt-in (`[flick] gates = false` by default); the default gate is a successful `cargo build --release --locked --offline` plus `codesign --verify`.
ASSUMPTION: HEAD builds export with `git archive` to ~/Library/Caches/Flick/rebuild/src and compile into `<source>/target/flick-rebuild`; the build log lives at ~/Library/Logs/Flick/rebuild.log.
ASSUMPTION: the in-app 'Rebuild Available' check runs on LauncherOpened/Wake at most every 30 s (`check_on_open = true`); there is no background polling.
acceptance: `scripts/check-all.sh` passes after every step; core coverage stays 100%; no file over 500 lines; release binary < 5 MB.

`flick flick version` on an app installed by `scripts/bundle.sh --install` prints the checkout's full HEAD sha, the build time, and `clean` or `dirty`; `defaults read ~/Applications/Flick.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleVersion` shows `0.0.1+<short sha>`.

After a new local commit, opening the launcher shows 'Rebuild Available' and the 'Flick Version' subtitle reads '1 commit newer in ~/Projects/flick: <subject>'; with installed == HEAD, no 'Rebuild Available' item.
'Rebuild Flick' with an uncommitted edit in the tree installs HEAD without that edit (stamp clean); 'Rebuild Flick (Dirty)' installs it and the stamp ends in `-dirty`.

During a build the `flick/build` view counts seconds and shows the last log line; `flick flick status` prints `building <n>s`; after the build Flick restarts and `pgrep -x Flick | wc -l` prints 1, with and without the launchd agent.
A build that fails (introduce a compile error, dirty build) leaves ~/Applications/Flick.app and the running process unchanged (same pid, same sha), opens rebuild.log, and shows 'Build failed'.
No network: a unit test pins the git subcommand allow-list (no fetch/pull/push/clone/remote); `grep -rE 'git.*(fetch|pull|push|clone)' src/` is empty; rebuild.log shows `--offline`.
`flick flick rebuild --source <agent worktree>` installs that worktree's HEAD and `flick flick version` reports its sha.
Accessibility stays granted across an in-app rebuild when an Apple Development identity exists (window snap works right after relaunch without a prompt).

Manual smoke: launcher opens; Flick Version subtitle correct; Rebuild (clean) → relaunch → version updated; Rebuild (Dirty) → `-dirty`; failed build → old app keeps running; Cancel Build stops cargo (`pgrep cargo` empty); `flick flick rebuild` from a terminal works while the launcher is closed.
Idle CPU ~0% over 60 s in Activity Monitor when no build runs (no timers added outside a running build).

name: Rebuild Flick from the local checkout

sections.context: Two background apps exist only to bend the keyboard, and Flick should replace both. (1) Hammerspoon runs one generated config, ~/.hammerspoon/init.lua (rendered by kota-voice src/trigger/hammerspoon.ts): an `hs.eventtap` on flagsChanged watches right-Command (keycode 54, device mask NX_DEVICERCMDKEYMASK 0x10) and right-Option (keycode 61, NX_DEVICERALTKEYMASK 0x40); when both are down it POSTs http://localhost:8600/pipeline/listen/start, when either is released it POSTs /pipeline/listen/stop (empty body, async, endpoints idempotent); it never swallows the keys; and a 5 s `hs.timer.doEvery` re-enables the tap because macOS silently disables long-lived taps after sleep, callback timeouts or TCC changes. Hammerspoon is installed only for this (homebrew cask in ~/.dotfiles/hosts/workstation.nix and mbp-server.nix). (2) Hyperkey (com.knollsoft.Hyperkey prefs on this machine: physicalKeycode=57 Caps Lock, keyRemap=1, hyperFlags=1966080 = 0x1E0000 = cmd|ctrl|alt|shift, executeQuickHyperKey=1, i.e. a quick press sends a key; launchOnLogin=1, hideMenuBarIcon=1) turns Caps Lock into Hyper. Flick's own config depends on it: ~/.dotfiles/home/.config/flick/config.toml binds window keys on Hyper (`left-half = "cmd+ctrl+alt+shift+KeyH"`, right-half L, maximize K, hide J, next-display N, previous-display P) through Carbon hotkeys (global-hotkey crate, src/platform/hotkeys.rs). The README roadmap already lists 'Triggers ... hold-a-modifier triggers, to replace small Hammerspoon configs'. One shared event tap in Flick removes two always-running apps and keeps all key behavior in one dotfiles-managed config.
sections.approach:
Module `keys` (src/modules/keys/, registry line `mod keys => "keys", keys::Keys::default;`, placed after `clip`), over one shared CGEventTap in the platform layer and a pure engine in core. Three layers, each its own step, so they can be built and tested in parallel:

1. Core engine (`src/core/keys.rs`, pure, 100% covered): `KeyName` parser (`caps_lock`, `right_cmd`, `left_alt`, `right_alt`, `right_ctrl`, `right_shift`, `fn`, `cmd`/`alt`/`ctrl`/`shift` = either side, plus the global-hotkey names `KeyA`, `Space`, `Escape`, `F18`, ... mapped to macOS virtual keycodes); `TapEvent { kind: Down|Up|FlagsChanged, keycode: u16, flags: u64, autorepeat: bool, injected: bool }`; `Rules { hyper: Option<Hyper { source: keycode, flags: u64, tap: Option<keycode>, tap_ms: u32 }>, chords: Vec<Chord { mods: u64 /* device-dependent masks */, key: Option<keycode> }> }`; `Engine::process(&mut self, ev, now_ms) -> Output { verdict: Pass | Drop | SetFlags(u64), inject: Option<keycode>, transitions: Vec<(u16 /*chord index*/, bool /*down*/)> }` and `Engine::resync(current_flags) -> transitions` (fires `up` for any chord no longer held, used after re-arm). Chord semantics copy init.lua exactly: active when every modifier's device bit is set (left keys never match a right_* chord) and the optional key is down; fire down once on entry, up once on exit; modifier events always pass through; a chord's non-modifier key is dropped (down, repeats, up) so it does not type; autorepeat never fires. Hyper: source key down → Drop, held = true; while held, every key/flags event passing through gets `SetFlags(flags | 0x1E0000)`; source up → Drop, and if no other key went down while held and held < tap_ms, `inject = tap`. Also `Event::Chord { index: u16, down: bool }` (Event stays Copy; serializes `{"event":"chord","index":0,"down":true}`, so `flick events` can also drive external tools).

2. Platform tap (`src/platform/keytap.rs`): one active `CGEventTapCreate(kCGSessionEventTap, kCGHeadInsertEventTap, kCGEventTapOptionDefault, keyDown|keyUp|flagsChanged)` on a dedicated thread with its own CFRunLoop, so a busy main thread (app scan, panel render) can never make the tap time out and stall system keyboard input. API: `keytap::start(handler: Box<dyn FnMut(TapEvent) -> TapOutput + Send>)`, `keytap::stop()`, `keytap::status() -> Running | NoPermission | Disabled`, `keytap::post_key(keycode)` (synthetic down+up stamped with a magic `kCGEventSourceUserData` so the tap marks it `injected` and passes it), `keytap::current_flags()` (`CGEventSourceFlagsState`), `keytap::secure_input()` (`IsSecureEventInputEnabled`). Re-arm: in the callback, `kCGEventTapDisabledByTimeout`/`ByUserInput` re-enable at once; a 5 s CFRunLoopTimer on the tap thread checks `CGEventTapIsEnabled` and re-enables (and re-creates the tap if creation had failed for lack of permission, so granting Accessibility later needs no restart); after any re-arm it calls a resync hook. Permission: active keyboard taps need Accessibility (Flick already asks for it); `AXIsProcessTrusted` gates creation; status is reported, never a modal. The tap exists only while rules are non-empty: no chords and no hyper means no tap, no timer, zero cost. The handler runs on the tap thread and only does the engine call plus a non-blocking `events::post` of transitions; no locks shared with the main thread except a short `Mutex<Rules>` swap on reload.

3. Caps Lock remap (`src/platform/hid.rs`): a CGEventTap cannot suppress the Caps Lock toggle (the LED and lock state change below it), so, like Hyperkey, remap at the HID layer: `hidutil property --get UserKeyMapping`, merge in `{Src: 0x700000039 (Caps Lock), Dst: 0x70000006D (F18, macOS keycode 79)}`, `--set` the merged list; `clear()` removes only Flick's entry. Called on enable/reload and from an `applicationWillTerminate` hook (new `platform::app::on_terminate`). The engine's hyper source is then F18 (79). `hyper = "caps_lock"` implies the remap; `hyper = "F18"` (or any key) skips it, for users who remap elsewhere.

4. Module + actions (`src/modules/keys/`): config `[keys] hyper = "caps_lock" | "<key>" | ""` (default "": off), `hyper_mods = "cmd+ctrl+alt+shift"`, `hyper_tap = "Escape" | ""`, `hyper_tap_ms = 300`, and `[[keys.chord]] name, keys = ["right_cmd", "right_alt"], on_down = { http = "POST http://localhost:8600/pipeline/listen/start" } | { shell = "..." }, on_up = {...}`. Actions run on one FIFO worker thread per module (so `stop` never overtakes `start`), never on the tap or main thread: `http` is a ~60-line HTTP/1.1 client on `std::net::TcpStream` (http:// only, `Content-Length: 0` for POST, `Connection: close`, 2 s connect/read timeout, response status logged; no new crate, binary stays < 5 MB); `shell` is `/bin/sh -c` spawned with `FLICK_CHORD=<name>` and `FLICK_CHORD_STATE=down|up`, not waited on by the worker (a reaper thread collects exit codes to the log). Verbs: `flick keys list` (chords and hyper with status), `flick keys status` (tap Running/NoPermission/Disabled, secure input on/off, HID remap set/not set, conflicts), `flick keys fire <name> down|up` (runs actions without the tap; used by step 4's tests and for scripting). One root item 'Key Triggers' whose subtitle shows the status ('Accessibility needed', 'Secure input is on: hyper paused').

5. Wiring: `configure` builds `core::keys::Rules` and starts/stops/updates the tap and HID remap; `on_event(Event::Chord{..})` enqueues the chord's action; `Event::Wake` triggers `resync` (fires `up` for a chord that was held across sleep, so kota-voice never stays listening). Conflict checks at configure time, reported in `flick keys status` and the log: Hyperkey.app running (bundle id com.knollsoft.Hyperkey) together with `hyper = "caps_lock"` (double remap); Hammerspoon running with a chord configured (duplicate start/stop: harmless because the endpoints are idempotent, but reported); hyper source key also bound as a global hotkey; a chord whose non-modifier key equals a bound global hotkey. Carbon hotkeys stay as they are: Hyper+H reaches the existing `[window.keys]` bindings because the tap rewrites the flags before Carbon matches them (step 2's spike verifies this first).

Parallelism: steps 1 (core engine), 2 (platform tap), 3 (HID remap) and 4 (module config + actions + verbs, no tap) touch disjoint files and can run concurrently. Step 5 wires them and needs all four. Step 6 (docs, DEFAULT_CONFIG, dotfiles snippet, smoke and cutover) is last. To keep `check-all.sh` green while a pub item is unused until step 5, steps 1-3 mark it `#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = "wired in flick-d717 step 5"))]`; step 5 removes the attributes (an unfulfilled expect fails lint, which enforces the cleanup).

Defaults chosen for open questions: Hyper sets flags on passing events (Hyperkey's model, hyperFlags 0x1E0000) rather than posting four synthetic modifier key-downs, so a tap-to-Escape never has to unwind fake modifiers; tap = Escape when released within 300 ms with no other key; chords pass their modifiers through like init.lua; hyper is off in DEFAULT_CONFIG and enabled in the user's dotfiles config; the module id is `keys` to match the seed's `[[keys.chord]]`.

alternatives.name: Keep Hammerspoon for push-to-talk and only add hyper
alternatives.rejected_because: Leaves a Lua runtime and a second event tap running for one 50-line script; the seed's goal is to remove Hammerspoon and Hyperkey.

alternatives.name: Carbon RegisterEventHotKey (global-hotkey) for chords
alternatives.rejected_because: Carbon hotkeys need a non-modifier key, fire on press only (no release, so no push-to-talk stop), and cannot tell right-Command from left-Command.

alternatives.name: Tap on the main run loop
alternatives.rejected_because: An active tap blocks all keyboard input while its callback waits; any main-thread stall (app rescan, panel draw, SQLite) would freeze typing system-wide and trip kCGEventTapDisabledByTimeout. A dedicated thread isolates it.

alternatives.name: Handle Caps Lock in the tap without a HID remap
alternatives.rejected_because: Caps Lock's lock state and LED toggle below the CGEventTap; dropping the flagsChanged event does not stop the toggle, so typing turns uppercase. Hyperkey and Karabiner both remap at the HID layer.

alternatives.name: Synthetic modifier key-down/up events for hyper
alternatives.rejected_because: Every tap or interrupted hold must post matching key-ups or modifiers stick; flag rewriting has no state outside the tap and matches Hyperkey's hyperFlags model.

alternatives.name: Listen-only tap plus a separate active tap for hyper
alternatives.rejected_because: Two taps double the re-arm and permission paths; the seed asks for one shared tap. A listen-only tap also needs Input Monitoring, a second TCC grant.

alternatives.name: HTTP actions via curl or a crate (ureq/reqwest)
alternatives.rejected_because: curl adds a process spawn per key edge; a crate adds binary size and TLS the use case does not need (localhost http). A small std TcpStream client covers it.

alternatives.name: IOHIDEventSystemClientSetProperty FFI for the Caps Lock remap
alternatives.rejected_because: Same effect as `hidutil property --set UserKeyMapping` but more unsafe code; hidutil ships with macOS. Revisit only if spawning hidutil proves slow or unreliable.

steps.title: Core: pure key engine (core::keys) with key names, Rules, chord + hyper state machine, resync, tap-to-key; Event::Chord { index, down }

Platform: one shared active CGEventTap on a dedicated run-loop thread with 5 s re-arm, Accessibility status, injected-event marker, post_key, current_flags, secure_input; spike that tap-rewritten flags still trigger Carbon hotkeys
Platform: Caps Lock to F18 HID remap via hidutil UserKeyMapping (merge, clear only our entry) and an on_terminate hook that clears it
Module `keys`: [keys] + [[keys.chord]] config, FIFO action worker (std TcpStream HTTP, shell), `flick keys list|status|fire`, Key Triggers status item (no tap yet)

Wire keys: configure installs Rules in the tap and the HID remap; Event::Chord runs actions; Wake/re-arm resync releases held chords; conflict checks (Hyperkey, Hammerspoon, hotkeys on the hyper source key)

Docs + cutover: README Keys/Triggers section and network note, ARCHITECTURE (keytap thread, hid, Event::Chord), DEFAULT_CONFIG examples, dotfiles snippet for kota-voice PTT; manual smoke and Hammerspoon/Hyperkey removal checklist

risks: Permissions: an active keyboard tap needs Accessibility; without it `CGEventTapCreate` returns NULL. Flick already has the grant, but an ad-hoc-signed rebuild resets it. Mitigation: status 'Accessibility needed' in the Key Triggers item and `flick keys status`; the 5 s timer retries creation, so a later grant works without a restart. Do not use a listen-only tap (it needs Input Monitoring, a second grant).

Event-tap timeouts: macOS disables a tap whose callback is slow (kCGEventTapDisabledByTimeout) and after sleep or TCC changes, silently. Mitigation: dedicated tap thread, engine call is O(chords) with no allocation on the hot path, immediate re-enable in the callback, 5 s health timer (same as init.lua's tapHealer), resync after re-arm.

Stuck push-to-talk: if the tap is disabled or the Mac sleeps while right-cmd+right-opt is held, the up edge is lost and kota-voice keeps listening. Mitigation: `Engine::resync(current_flags)` after every re-arm and on Event::Wake fires the missing `up`.

Secure input (password fields, Terminal 'Secure Keyboard Entry', some password managers) hides keyDown/keyUp from taps: hyper and key chords stop working there; modifier-only chords (flagsChanged) still work. Mitigation: `keytap::secure_input()` shown in status; documented as a known limit (Hyperkey has the same one).

Caps Lock left dead: the hidutil mapping outlives Flick. If Flick crashes, Caps Lock stays F18 until Flick restarts (launchd KeepAlive restarts it) or logout. Mitigation: clear on quit and on `hyper` turned off; document `hidutil property --set '{"UserKeyMapping":[]}'` as the manual reset. hidutil's UserKeyMapping is one global list: read-merge-write so other mappings survive.

Double remap: Hyperkey.app and Flick both remapping Caps Lock gives unpredictable results. Mitigation: conflict check on bundle id com.knollsoft.Hyperkey; cutover order in step 6 is quit Hyperkey (and turn off its launchOnLogin) before enabling `hyper`.

Carbon hotkey interaction: the existing `[window.keys]` Hyper bindings must still fire when Hyper comes from the tap. Session-tap flag rewriting should be seen by Carbon hotkey matching (Hyperkey works this way), but step 2 verifies it first with a spike; fallback if it fails: post synthetic modifier events (the rejected alternative) behind the same engine output.

Key-repeat: holding Caps Lock (F18) autorepeats keyDown; holding a chord key repeats too. Mitigation: the engine ignores events with kCGKeyboardEventAutorepeat for state changes and drops repeats of the hyper source and chord keys; tests cover it.
Conflicts with global-hotkey bindings: a Carbon hotkey on F18 or on a chord's key would also fire. Mitigation: configure-time check reports it; README warns.
Feedback loops: the injected Escape re-enters the tap. Mitigation: mark synthetic events with kCGEventSourceUserData and pass them untouched.

Network promise: README says Flick 'sends nothing over the network'. HTTP actions only go to URLs the user configures; README wording changes to say so. http:// only, no TLS, 2 s timeouts so a dead kota-voice never blocks the worker for long.

Lint across steps: pub items unused until step 5 fail `dead_code`; use the `cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason))` pattern and remove it in step 5. Do not add expect attributes for expect/unwrap/panic lints in test code (mulch mx-db1a9b, mx-7376a8).
Main-thread borrow: Event::Chord arrives via events::post; `app::on_event` already re-queues on BorrowMutError (mulch mx-fcbc43). Actions must not run inside on_event beyond a channel send.
check:size and coverage: core/ has a 100% line-coverage floor; the engine must be fully unit tested. Keep keytap.rs, hid.rs and each module file under 500 lines (mulch mx-e7e3ab).

Unsafe surface: CGEventTap callbacks are `extern "C"` with a raw user-info pointer; keep every unsafe block in src/platform with a SAFETY comment (clippy undocumented_unsafe_blocks, multiple_unsafe_ops_per_block).
ASSUMPTION: Caps Lock is remapped to F18 (HID 0x70000006D, keycode 79) with hidutil, not handled directly in the tap; `hyper = "F18"` lets a user skip the remap.
ASSUMPTION: Hyper adds cmd|ctrl|alt|shift (0x1E0000, matching Hyperkey's hyperFlags=1966080) to passing events instead of posting synthetic modifier key events.

ASSUMPTION: a Caps Lock tap sends Escape when released within 300 ms with no other key pressed (`hyper_tap_ms = 300`, `hyper_tap = ""` turns it off). Hyperkey's exact quick-press timing is unknown; 300 ms is the default.
ASSUMPTION: chords pass their modifiers through to apps (as init.lua returns false); a chord's non-modifier key, if any, is swallowed.

ASSUMPTION: hyper is off and no chords exist in DEFAULT_CONFIG (no tap, no permission prompt for users who do not opt in); the user's dotfiles config enables `hyper = "caps_lock"` and the kota-voice chord.
ASSUMPTION: HTTP actions support http:// only (localhost use case); https is out of scope until a user needs it.
ASSUMPTION: Event::Chord carries the chord's index, not its name, so Event stays Copy; `flick keys list` maps index to name.
acceptance: `scripts/check-all.sh` passes after every step; `src/core/` stays at 100% line coverage; `unsafe`/CoreGraphics code only in src/platform (check:layers); release binary < 5 MB.

Engine unit tests cover: right_cmd+right_alt chord fires down once and up once on releasing either key; left cmd/alt never fire it; autorepeat never fires; hyper sets 0x1E0000 on H while held; Caps-tap within 300 ms yields Escape, a hold with H yields no Escape; resync releases a held chord; injected events pass untouched.

With `[[keys.chord]] name = "ptt", keys = ["right_cmd","right_alt"], on_down = { http = "POST http://localhost:8600/pipeline/listen/start" }, on_up = { http = "POST http://localhost:8600/pipeline/listen/stop" }`, holding both keys starts kota-voice listening and releasing either stops it, with Hammerspoon quit (verify in kota-voice logs, or with `nc -l 8600` showing exactly one start and one stop request per press).
`flick events` prints `{"event":"chord","index":0,"down":true}` then `..."down":false}` for one press; `flick keys fire ptt down` sends the start request without touching the keyboard.

With `hyper = "caps_lock"` and Hyperkey quit: Caps Lock+H/L/K/J/N/P run left-half/right-half/maximize/hide/next-display/previous-display from the existing `[window.keys]` config; a Caps Lock tap sends Escape (closes a dialog / exits vim insert mode); Caps Lock never toggles uppercase; holding Caps Lock+L repeats and cycles 1/2 → 2/3 → 1/3.
After sleep/wake, and after `tccutil`-style revoke and re-grant of Accessibility, chords and hyper work again within 5 s without restarting Flick; `flick keys status` reports Running.
Quitting Flick (Quit Flick) restores Caps Lock: `hidutil property --get UserKeyMapping` no longer lists 0x700000039; turning `hyper` off and reloading does the same.
In a secure-input field (Terminal with Secure Keyboard Entry on), `flick keys status` shows secure input on; the right-cmd+right-opt chord still works there.
`flick keys status` reports a conflict when Hyperkey.app is running with `hyper = "caps_lock"`, and when Hammerspoon is running with a chord configured.

Manual smoke: launcher hotkey, window switcher, desktop toggle and all Hyper window keys work; typing in an editor is unaffected (no dropped or doubled keys, cmd+H/L still work in apps); push-to-talk works 20 times in a row; Escape tap works; Caps Lock LED never lights; Flick restart via launchd keeps everything working.
With no `[keys]` table (DEFAULT_CONFIG), no tap is created (`flick keys status` says 'off') and no hidutil mapping is set.
Idle CPU ~0% over 60 s in Activity Monitor with hyper and a chord enabled (only the 5 s re-arm timer runs); typing latency is not noticeable.
Cutover: Hammerspoon and Hyperkey can be quit and removed from login items (and the hammerspoon cask from the dotfiles hosts) with no lost behavior; step 6 documents the dotfiles config snippet.
